jurisdictions.name: Ankeny
jurisdictions.portal_name: Online permit application (Apply For Permit link)
notes: Ankeny's pool handout requires a building permit for all swimming pools, a site plan showing the pool, decks, the barrier, easements, drainage, well and septic, and one set of pool construction drawings or manufacturer specifications.
The handout requires a detailed drawing of the pool barrier, and separate permits for the fence, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work.
Under the city code section quoted in the handout, residential pools go in the side or rear yard, at least 4 ft from any property line, and outdoor pools must be enclosed by a barrier.
Ankeny lists the 2024 I-codes with amendments effective July 1, 2025, including its own 2024 Swimming Pool and Spa Code (Municipal Code Chapter 183).

sources.title: Swimming Pools - Residential Guidelines, City of Ankeny

jurisdictions.name: Davenport
notes: Davenport takes plans and applications through its E-Plan portal and accepts only unsecured PDF files, with drawings uploaded as individual vector-based PDFs.

The city's permit guide exempts prefabricated pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy only if they are less than 24 inches deep and not over 5,000 gallons; they must still meet fencing and enclosure rules.
Other pools fall under general building improvements and need a building permit.

sources.title: Electronic Plan Review - City of Davenport
What Does/Does Not Require a Permit? - City of Davenport

jurisdictions.name: Urbandale
notes: Urbandale applicants create an account in its cloud-based Permit Portal to apply, follow the review and track the permit through final inspection.
The city's Building Codes page lists the 2018 International Building Code and 2018 International Residential Code.

sources.title: Permits - Other Residential - City of Urbandale
